questions.question: What is the overdue limit for microfinance lending as per the Microfinance Industry Network directives, effective January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹3,000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Microfinance Industry Network (MFIN)** and **Sa-Dhan**, which are the two **Self-Regulatory Organizations (SROs)** for the microfinance sector in **India**, have jointly issued a revised **Code of Conduct** and directives to enhance credit discipline.
 
• As per the new directives, any borrower who has an **overdue amount** exceeding **₹3,000** will not be eligible for a **fresh loan** or a top-up loan from any microfinance lender.
 
• These measures, often referred to as **"guardrails"**, are designed to prevent **over-leveraging** and **indebtedness** among low-income households, ensuring that the borrower's debt remains at a manageable level.
 
• This specific directive regarding the **₹3,000 overdue limit** is set to become **effective from January 1, 2025**.
 
• The decision was taken in response to rising concerns about **asset quality** and high **delinquency rates** in certain geographical pockets within the **microfinance industry**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Household Income Limit:** According to **RBI guidelines** issued in **March 2022**, a microfinance loan is defined as a **collateral-free loan** to a household having an **annual income** up to **₹3,00,000**.
 
• **Total Indebtedness Cap:** The **SROs** have mandated that the **total indebtedness** of a single borrower across all lenders should not exceed **₹2,00,000**. This includes both **principal** and **interest** components of all active loans.
 
• **Number of Lenders:** To curb the practice of **ghost lending** or multiple borrowing, a **borrower** is restricted to taking loans from a maximum of **four different lenders** (including **NBFC-MFIs**, Banks, and Small Finance Banks) at any given point in time.
 
• **Regulatory Oversight:** The **Microfinance Industry Network (MFIN)** was established in **2009** and serves as the primary **SRO** recognized by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to monitor **NBFC-MFIs**.
 
• **The 50% Rule:** Lenders must ensure that the **outflow** for all loan repayments (including principal and interest) does not exceed **50%** of the **monthly household income** of the borrower.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Delinquency Monitoring:** The **overdue limit** is calculated based on data from **Credit Information Companies (CICs)** like **Equifax** or **CRIF High Mark**, which lenders are required to consult before every disbursement.
 
• **Scope of Applicability:** These directives apply to all **regulated entities (REs)** including **Banks**, **Small Finance Banks (SFBs)**, and **Non-Banking Financial Company-Microfinance Institutions (NBFC-MFIs)**.
 
• **Effective Implementation:** While the **₹3,000 overdue rule** starts in **January 2025**, other guardrails regarding **income assessment** and **disclosure of pricing** were reinforced throughout **2024**.
 
• **Social Impact:** The **microfinance sector** in India serves nearly **8 crore** unique borrowers, and these rules are critical to maintaining the **socio-economic stability** of the **rural** and **semi-urban** population.

questions.question: The revised roadmap released in June 2025 for the National Mission for Green India (GIM) places special emphasis on ecological restoration in which of the following critical regions?

options.text: Aravalli Range, Western Ghats, Himalayas, and mangroves

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aravalli Range, Western Ghats, Himalayas, and mangroves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Mission for Green India (GIM)** released a revised roadmap in **June 2025** to align with India's updated **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC)** and biodiversity goals.
 
• The roadmap identifies the **Aravalli Range** as a critical zone for restoration to act as a "green barrier" against the eastward expansion of the **Thar Desert** and to combat **land degradation**.
 
• Special emphasis is placed on the **Western Ghats** and the **Himalayas**, which are globally recognized **biodiversity hotspots**, to ensure **water security** and stabilize fragile mountain ecosystems against **climate change**.
 
• The restoration of **mangroves** along India's coastline is prioritized due to their exceptional capacity for **carbon sequestration** and their role as natural buffers against **cyclones** and sea-level rise.
 
• The revised strategy shifts focus from mere afforestation to **Ecological Restoration**, which involves reviving the original structure and function of degraded ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Mission for Green India (GIM):**
 
 
• Launched in **February 2014**, it is one of the **eight missions** under the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)**.
 
• Its primary objective is to protect, restore, and enhance India's diminishing forest cover and respond to climate change.
 
• The mission aims at increasing forest/tree cover to the extent of **5 million hectares (mha)** and improving the quality of forest cover on another **5 mha** of non-forest/forest lands.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Focus Areas:**
 
 
• The **Aravalli Range** spans across **Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana,** and **Delhi**, serving as the "lungs" of the **National Capital Region (NCR)**.
 
• The **Western Ghats** runs along the western coast of India through six states: **Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala,** and **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• **Mangrove** restoration specifically targets regions like the **Sundarbans** in **West Bengal** and the **Bhitarkanika** in **Odisha**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Implementation Agency:** The mission is implemented by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** through a decentralized structure involving **State Forest Departments** and local bodies.
 
• **Community Involvement:** A unique feature of the roadmap is the empowerment of **Gram Sabhas** and **Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMCs)** to lead restoration efforts at the grassroots level.
 
• **Climate Targets:** India aims to create an additional carbon sink of **2.5 to 3 billion tonnes** of **CO2 equivalent** through additional forest and tree cover by **2030**.
 
• **Monitoring Technology:** The **2025 roadmap** integrates advanced technologies such as **Geographic Information Systems (GIS)**, **Remote Sensing**, and **Lidar** for real-time monitoring of survival rates and biomass growth.
</ul

questions.question: The sixth phase of the ‘Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain 2025’ was launched in which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sixth phase** of the **Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain (JSA:CTR) 2025** was launched by the **President of India**, **Droupadi Murmu**.
 
• The official launch ceremony took place on **February 12, 2025**, in the state of **Haryana**.
 
• The event was organized at the **National Institute of Food Technology Entrepreneurship and Management (NIFTEM)** located in **Kundli**, **Sonipat** district.
 
• The **2025 campaign** aims to consolidate the gains of previous phases and intensify **water conservation** efforts across the country before the arrival of the **monsoon season**.
 
• The focus of this phase is on the **sustainability of water sources** and ensuring that every drop of rainwater is harvested through community participation and **Panchayati Raj Institutions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jal Shakti Abhiyan (JSA):**
 
 
• The mission was first launched in **2019** as a time-bound, mission-mode **water conservation** campaign in **256 water-stressed districts** of India.
 
• In **2021**, it was expanded to cover all districts (rural and urban) under the theme **"Catch the Rain, where it falls, when it falls"**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Jal Shakti:**
 
 
• This ministry was created in **May 2019** by merging two existing ministries: the **Ministry of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation** and the **Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation**.
 
• The ministry oversees major flagship schemes like **Jal Jeevan Mission** and **Namami Gange**.
 
 
 
• **Haryana's Water Initiatives:**
 
 
• The state of **Haryana** has been a pioneer in water management through schemes like **Mera Pani Meri Virasat**, which incentivizes farmers to switch from water-intensive **paddy** to other crops like **maize** or **pulses**.
 
• The state has also implemented the **Atal Bhujal Yojana** extensively to tackle declining **groundwater levels**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Five Pillars of JSA:CTR:**
 
 
• The campaign is built on five key interventions: **water conservation and rainwater harvesting**, **renovation of traditional water bodies** (like ponds/talabs), **reuse and recharge of borewells**, **watershed development**, and **intensive afforestation**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 6th Phase:**
 
 
• The **2025 phase** emphasizes **geo-tagging** of all water bodies and the creation of **Jal Shakti Kendras** in every district to provide technical guidance to the public.
 
• It also integrates the **"Amrit Sarovar"** mission, which aims to develop and rejuvenate **75 water bodies** in each district as part of the **Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav**.
 
 
 
• **National Importance:**
 
 
• India possesses nearly **18%** of the world's population but only **4%** of the world's **renewable water resources**, making campaigns like **Catch the Rain** critical for **national water security**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: In late November 2025, which cyclonic storm prompted the IMD to issue warnings for north Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and adjoining south Andhra Pradesh, and made landfall around 30 November 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cyclone Ditwah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cyclone Ditwah** was a tropical cyclone that developed in the **Bay of Bengal** during the late **November 2025** period.
 
• The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** monitored the system as it intensified from a deep depression into a **Cyclonic Storm**, moving towards the southeastern coast of **India**.
 
• The storm made its **landfall** around **30 November 2025**, specifically impacting the coastal stretches of **north Tamil Nadu** and the Union Territory of **Puducherry**.
 
• Red and orange alerts were issued for several districts, including **Chennai**, **Chengalpattu**, and **Villupuram**, as the storm brought **heavy to very heavy rainfall** and strong gale winds.
 
• The administrative machinery in **south Andhra Pradesh** was also put on high alert to manage potential **storm surges** and flooding in districts such as **Nellore** and **Tirupati**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Naming Mechanism**: Tropical cyclones in the **North Indian Ocean** are named by the **WMO/ESCAP** Panel on Tropical Cyclones, which consists of **13 member countries**. The name **Ditwah** was contributed by **Yemen**, following the **169-name** list established in **2020**.
 
• **Geographic Context**: The **Bay of Bengal** is known for a higher frequency of cyclones compared to the **Arabian Sea**. This is primarily due to higher **sea surface temperatures** and the shape of the coastline, which funnels storms toward **India** and **Bangladesh**.
 
• **IMD Classification**: The **India Meteorological Department** classifies tropical systems based on **Maximum Sustained Surface Wind (MSW)**. A **Cyclonic Storm** has wind speeds between **62 km/h and 88 km/h**, while a **Severe Cyclonic Storm** reaches **89 km/h to 117 km/h**.
 
• **Post-Monsoon Season**: The months of **October**, **November**, and **December** comprise the peak season for cyclonic activity in the **North Indian Ocean**, often coinciding with the **Northeast Monsoon** in southern **India**.
 
• **Landfall Definition**: **Landfall** occurs when the eye of the storm moves over the land. It is usually the most destructive phase due to the combined impact of **storm surges**, **extreme wind speeds**, and **torrential rain**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Disaster Management**: In anticipation of **Cyclone Ditwah**, the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** and state disaster teams were pre-positioned in vulnerable coastal areas to facilitate **rescue** and **relief** operations.
 
• **Monitoring Technology**: The **IMD** utilized **Dopler Weather Radars (DWR)** located at **Chennai** and **Sriharikota** to provide real-time updates and track the **trajectory** of the cyclone with high precision.
 
• **Impact on Infrastructure**: Cyclonic storms like **Ditwah** often lead to the suspension of **flight operations**, disruption of **railway services**, and damage to **power grids** and **telecommunication** towers in the impacted zones.
 
• **Climate Trends**: Scientific observations indicate that while the total number of cyclones remains relatively stable, the **intensity** of storms in the **Bay of Bengal** has been increasing due to **global warming** and rising **ocean heat content**.
</ul

questions.question: Which Indian javelin thrower won gold at the Taiwan Athletics Open in June 2025?

__
 
• Indian javelin thrower **Rohit Yadav** secured the **Gold Medal** at the **Taiwan Athletics Open**, delivering an impressive performance on the international stage.
 
• He achieved a best throw of **83.28 meters** during the competition, which took place at the **Banqiao Stadium** in **New Taipei City**.
 
• This victory was significant as it marked a successful return for the **23-year-old** athlete following a major **elbow surgery** in **2023** that had sidelined him from the **Asian Games** and **World Championships**.
 
• The **Taiwan Athletics Open** serves as a crucial **World Athletics Continental Tour (Bronze)** event, providing athletes with valuable ranking points for major championships like the **Olympics**.
 
• By clinching the **Gold**, **Rohit Yadav** solidified his position as one of India's premier javelin throwers, trailing only behind elite athletes like **Neeraj Chopra** and **Kishore Jena** in recent seasons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Neeraj Chopra**:
 
 
• He is the most decorated Indian javelin thrower, winning the **Gold Medal** at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics** with a throw of **87.58 meters**.
 
• In **2023**, he became the first Indian to win a **Gold Medal** at the **World Athletics Championships** held in **Budapest**.
 
 
 
• **Kishore Jena**:
 
 
• Hailing from **Odisha**, he emerged as a world-class competitor by winning the **Silver Medal** at the **19th Asian Games** in **Hangzhou**.
 
• He achieved a personal best of **87.54 meters**, which is one of the highest marks ever recorded by an Indian.
 
 
 
• **Athletics Federation of India (AFI)**:
 
 
• It is the apex body for athletics in the **Republic of India**, responsible for selecting athletes for the **Olympics** and other international competitions.
 
• The federation was established in **1946** and is headquartered in **New Delhi**.
 
 
 
• **Davinder Singh Kang**:
 
 
• He was the first Indian javelin thrower to reach the final of the **World Athletics Championships**, achieving this feat in **2017** in **London**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Performance Data**: The winning throw of **83.28 meters** by **Rohit Yadav** in **Taiwan** was his second-best career performance at that time, following his personal best of **83.40 meters** recorded in **2022**.
 
• **National Context**: India has seen a "Javelin Revolution" following **Neeraj Chopra's** success, with multiple athletes consistently crossing the **80-meter** mark in **national** and **international** meets.
 
• **Technical Specs**: In international athletics, the men's javelin must weigh **800 grams** and measures between **2.6 to 2.7 meters** in length. The competition usually involves **six attempts** for the finalists.
 
• **Venue Details**: The **Banqiao Stadium** is a multi-purpose stadium in **Taiwan** with a capacity of approximately **30,000** people, frequently hosting **Track and Field** events.
</ul

questions.question: The National Red List Assessment Initiative, launched in India in October 2025, aligns with IUCN global standards and supports the country’s commitments under which of the following international frameworks?

options.text: Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Red List Assessment Initiative** was launched in **India** in **October 2025** to systematically evaluate the conservation status of various species within the country's territory.
 
• This initiative is designed to align strictly with the **IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature)** global standards, which provide a rigorous objective framework for classifying species according to their **extinction risk**.
 
• A primary objective of this national assessment is to fulfill **India’s** international obligations under the **Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF)**, which was adopted to halt and reverse biodiversity loss. ***Hence, the correct answer is Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.***
 
• The initiative is a collaborative effort involving the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**, the **Zoological Survey of India (ZSI)**, and the **Botanical Survey of India (BSI)**.
 
• By creating a **National Red List**, India aims to prioritize conservation efforts for **endangered** and **threatened** species, ensuring that resource allocation is based on scientific data and urgent ecological needs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF):**
 
 
• Adopted during the **15th Conference of Parties (COP15)** to the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)** in **December 2022**.
 
• It consists of **4 overarching goals** for **2050** and **23 targets** to be achieved by **2030**.
 
• **Target 4** specifically focuses on halting human-induced **extinction** of known threatened species and promoting their recovery and conservation.
 
• This framework is often referred to as the "**Paris Agreement for Nature**," emphasizing its importance in global environmental governance.
 
 
 
• **IUCN Red List Categories:**
 
 
• The assessment uses specific categories such as **Extinct (EX)**, **Critically Endangered (CR)**, **Endangered (EN)**, **Vulnerable (VU)**, and **Near Threatened (NT)**.
 
• Species classified as **CR, EN, or VU** are collectively referred to as "**threatened**" species.
 
• The **National Red List** allows for a more localized understanding of species that might be common globally but are **threatened** within **India**.
 
 
 
• **Other Frameworks Mentioned:**
 
 
• The **Sendai Framework** is focused on **Disaster Risk Reduction** (2015-2030) and is not primarily a biodiversity assessment tool.
 
• The **Ramsar Convention** focuses specifically on the conservation and sustainable use of **wetlands**.
 
• **Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Frameworks** generally relate to climate change mitigation under the **UNFCCC** rather than species-level biodiversity assessments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India's Biodiversity Status:** India is recognized as one of the **17 megadiverse countries** in the world, harboring nearly **7-8%** of the world’s recorded species while occupying only **2.4%** of the world’s land area.
 
• **Institutional Role:** The **Zoological Survey of India (ZSI)**, established in **1916**, and the **Botanical Survey of India (BSI)**, established in **1890**, serve as the premier organizations for taxonomic and biological studies in the country.
 
• **Legal Support:** The findings from the **National Red List Assessment Initiative** will likely influence the implementation of the **Biological Diversity Act, 2002**, and the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
 
• **National Biodiversity Targets (NBTs):** India has updated its **National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP)** to align with the **KMGBF**, ensuring that national actions contribute to **global biodiversity goals**.

questions.question: Which prodigious ice-hockey talent was awarded the EJ McGuire Award of Excellence, highlighting character and athleticism, ahead of the 2025 NHL Draft?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Michael Misa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Michael Misa**, a highly-rated forward for the **Saginaw Spirit** in the **Ontario Hockey League (OHL)**, was announced as the recipient of the **E.J. McGuire Award of Excellence** in **June 2024**.
 
• The award is presented annually by the **NHL Central Scouting** to the draft prospect who best exemplifies a **commitment to excellence** through **strength of character, competitiveness, and athleticism**.
 
• Misa is considered a top prospect for the **2025 NHL Draft**, making him one of the youngest and most prestigious talents to be recognized with this honor ahead of his eligibility year.
 
• In **2022**, he was granted **Exceptional Player Status** by **Hockey Canada**, allowing him to enter the **OHL** at the age of **15**, joining an elite group of players including **John Tavares**, **Connor McDavid**, and **Connor Bedard**.
 
• During the **2023-24 season**, he played a critical role in helping the **Saginaw Spirit** capture their first-ever **Memorial Cup** championship, further solidifying his reputation as a big-game performer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The E.J. McGuire Award of Excellence:**
 
 
• The award was established in **2011** to honor the legacy of **E.J. McGuire**, who served as the Director of the **NHL Central Scouting Bureau** from **2005 to 2011**.
 
• It aims to recognize the "personality of the draft," focusing on players who demonstrate **leadership** and **dedication** off the ice as much as their skills on it.
 
• Past winners of this prestigious award include **Connor Bedard** (2023), **Lane Hutson** (2022), **William Eklund** (2021), and **Nico Hischier** (2017).
 
 
 
• **Exceptional Player Status:**
 
 
• This designation is awarded by **Hockey Canada** to players who demonstrate the **physical, mental, and social maturity** to play major junior hockey a year early.
 
• **Michael Misa** became only the **sixth player** in **OHL history** to receive this status, following his record-breaking performance at the **OHL Cup** where he surpassed **Connor McDavid's** scoring record with **20 points** in seven games.
 
 
 
• **2025 NHL Draft Outlook:**
 
 
• The **2025 NHL Draft** is expected to feature **Misa** as a potential top-five selection due to his **elite skating**, **hockey IQ**, and consistent production in the **Canadian Hockey League (CHL)**.
 
• His early recognition with the **McGuire Award** highlights the **NHL's** scouting community's high regard for his **maturity** and **professionalism** at a young age.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following nutritional concerns are being highlighted in the food awareness campaign launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare on the occasion of World Food Safety Day, 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hidden sugars, fats and oils**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question: In March 2025, the Ministry of Environment Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) tightened emissions standards for which industry under the Environment (Protection) Second Amendment Rules, 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Caustic soda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **March 2025**, the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** issued a notification regarding the **Environment (Protection) Second Amendment Rules, 2025**, which specifically tightens the environmental standards for the **Caustic soda** industry.
 
• The **Caustic soda** sector, also known as the **chlor-alkali** industry, is one of the most chemically intensive industries, and the new rules aim to further reduce the discharge of **toxic effluents** and **gaseous emissions**.
 
• These rules introduce more stringent limits for parameters such as **Total Suspended Solids (TSS)**, **Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD)**, and **pH levels** in the wastewater discharged by these industrial units. ***Hence, the industry mentioned is Caustic soda.***
 
• The amendment specifically mandates the complete transition of any remaining legacy units to **Membrane Cell Technology** to eliminate **Mercury** traces in the environment, aligning with the **Minamata Convention** objectives.
 
• The **MoEFCC** exercises these powers under **Sections 6 and 25** of the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** to ensure that industrial growth does not come at the cost of ecological health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Caustic Soda (Sodium Hydroxide):**
 
 
• It is a vital industrial chemical (**NaOH**) used extensively in the manufacture of **soaps, detergents, paper, textiles**, and for **alumina refining** in the aluminum industry.
 
• The production process involves the electrolysis of **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)** brine, which simultaneously produces **Chlorine** gas and **Hydrogen** as by-products.
 
 
 
• **Industry Comparison:**
 
 
• While the **Cement** industry is a major source of **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)** and particulate matter, and the **Textile** industry is known for **dye-related water pollution**, the **2025 Second Amendment** specifically focuses on the chemical complexities of the **chlor-alkali** (Caustic soda) sector.
 
• The **Dairy** industry is regulated under different standards focusing primarily on organic waste and **Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD)**.
 
 
 
• **The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986:**
 
 
• This landmark **Act** of the **Parliament of India** was enacted in the wake of the **Bhopal Gas Tragedy** of **1984**.
 
• It provides a framework for the **Central Government** to coordinate the activities of various state and central authorities, such as the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technology Shift:** India has successfully mandated the shift from **Mercury Cell** technology to **Membrane Cell Technology** in the **Caustic soda** sector to prevent **Mercury poisoning**. The **2025** rules further refine the operational efficiency of these membranes.
 
• **Compliance and Penalties:** Industrial units found violating the standards set in the **Environment (Protection) Second Amendment Rules, 2025** are liable for penalties under **Section 15** of the **EPA, 1986**, which includes heavy fines and potential **imprisonment**.
 
• **Monitoring:** The **CPCB** and **State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)** are tasked with the continuous monitoring of these industries using **Online Continuous Effluent Monitoring Systems (OCEMS)** to ensure real-time data reporting to the ministry.
 
• **Global Context:** By tightening these standards in **2025**, **India** aims to meet its international commitments under various **climate and environment treaties**, ensuring that the "**Make in India**" initiative remains sustainable and eco-friendly.
</ul

questions.question: Which author/translator pair won the International Booker Prize, 2025, for Heart Lamp?
questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Banu Mushtaq and Deepa Bhasthi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Booker Prize** for the year **2025** has been awarded to the **Kannada** author **Banu Mushtaq** and the translator **Deepa Bhasthi** for the novel titled **Heart Lamp**.
 
• This prestigious award recognizes the finest in translated fiction from around the globe, ensuring that exceptional stories written in languages other than English reach a worldwide audience. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Banu Mushtaq** is the original author of the work, which was originally penned in **Kannada**, a language primarily spoken in the Indian state of **Karnataka**.
 
• **Deepa Bhasthi** is the **translator** who rendered the literary work into **English**, making it eligible for the international competition held in the **United Kingdom**.
 
• The prize includes a cash award of **£50,000** (approximately **53 lakh INR**), which is distributed **equally** between the author and the translator to honor the collaborative nature of the work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Banu Mushtaq:**
 
 
• She is a prominent **feminist writer**, **poet**, and **social activist** from **India**.
 
• Her writings often focus on the **lived experiences of women**, **social justice**, and **communal harmony** within the cultural landscape of **South India**.
 
• She has received several accolades in the past, including the **Karnataka Sahitya Academy Award**.
 
 
 
• **Deepa Bhasthi:**
 
 
• She is an **independent writer** and **editor** whose work frequently explores the intersections of **art**, **culture**, and **landscape**.
 
• As a translator, she has played a significant role in bringing **contemporary Kannada literature** to an English-speaking readership.
 
 
 
• **The International Booker Prize:**
 
 
• Established in **2005**, it was initially a biennial prize awarded to a living author for their entire body of work.
 
• Since **2016**, the format changed to an **annual prize** for a single book that is translated into **English** and published in the **UK** or **Ireland**.
 
• It is distinct from the **Booker Prize**, which is awarded to novels originally written in **English**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Context:**
 
 
• **Kiran Desai** is a world-renowned author who won the **Man Booker Prize** in **2006** for her novel **The Inheritance of Loss**.
 
• **David Szalay** is a **British-Canadian** novelist known for his work **All That Man Is**, which was shortlisted for the **Booker Prize** in **2016**.
 
• **Margaret Atwood** is a legendary **Canadian** author who has won the **Booker Prize** twice, in **2000** for **The Blind Assassin** and in **2019** for **The Testaments**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The win for **Heart Lamp** marks a significant milestone for **Indian literature**, following the success of **Geetanjali Shree** and **Daisy Rockwell**, who won the prize in **2022** for **Tomb of Sand** (originally **Ret Samadhi**).
 
• The selection process involves a **panel of five judges** who review a longlist and then a **six-book shortlist** before announcing the winner in a ceremony held in **London**.
 
• Translation prizes like these are essential for promoting **linguistic diversity** and encouraging publishers to invest in **non-Western narratives**.

questions.question: In May 2025, the RBI introduced a new Payments Regulatory Board of how many members to regulate and supervise payment systems in the country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** established the **Payments Regulatory Board (PRB)** to exercise the powers and perform the functions of the central bank in relation to the **regulation and supervision** of payment systems.
 
• The **Payments Regulatory Board** consists of **6 members** in total, designed to provide a balanced representation of central bank authority and external expertise.
 
• The **Governor of the Reserve Bank of India** serves as the **ex-officio Chairperson** of the Board, ensuring that payment policy remains aligned with broader monetary objectives.
 
• The composition includes the **Deputy Governor** in charge of the **Department of Payment and Settlement Systems** as a member, along with one **officer** of the **Reserve Bank** nominated by the **Central Board** of the **RBI**.
 
• To ensure a diverse perspective in the **fintech** and **digital banking** sectors, the **Central Government** nominates **three members** to the board.
 
• The primary mandate of this board is to oversee **retail and wholesale payment systems**, including **digital wallets**, **card networks**, and **online transaction gateways**, to ensure they operate in a safe and efficient manner.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Legislative Framework:** The formation of the **Payments Regulatory Board** was facilitated through amendments to the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**, particularly following the recommendations of the **Ratan Watal Committee** on digital payments.
 
• **Replacement of BPSS:** The **PRB** replaced the earlier **Board for Regulation and Supervision of Payment and Settlement Systems (BPSS)**, which was a sub-committee of the **Central Board** of the **RBI**.
 
• **Objective of Innovation:** One of the key goals of the **PRB** is to foster **competition** and **innovation** within the **financial technology (FinTech)** ecosystem while maintaining **financial stability**.
 
• **Interoperability:** The board is responsible for drafting policies that mandate **interoperability** between different payment service providers, such as **UPI** apps and **mobile wallets**, to enhance user convenience.
 
• **Consumer Protection:** A significant portion of the board's regulatory oversight is dedicated to **customer grievance redressal** and ensuring robust **cybersecurity** protocols to prevent **online fraud**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tenure of Members:** The members nominated by the **Central Government** typically hold office for a period of **3 years** and are eligible for re-appointment, providing continuity in policy making.
 
• **Governance Standards:** The board holds meetings at regular intervals, at least **once every quarter**, to review the status of the **national payment infrastructure** and the performance of **Systemically Important Payment Systems (SIPS)**.
 
• **Data Sovereignty:** Under the guidance of the **PRB**, the **RBI** enforces strict **data localization** norms, requiring payment companies to store **transaction data** of Indian citizens on servers located within **India**.
 
• **Global Alignment:** The **PRB** works to ensure that **Indian payment systems** comply with international standards set by the **Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures (CPMI)** and the **Bank for International Settlements (BIS)**.
</ul
